name: Nostoi
tagline: Let the record outlive the system.
description: Tamper-evident audit chains for systems whose actions must remain open to examination. Nostoi verifies recorded history, identifies the first inconsistency, and supports checkpoints and signed statements beyond the producer's own account of events.
status: Active development · verifier, CLI and TUI in source; registry publication pending
motifCaption: The homecoming: a chain carried safely across the river.

demonstration.label: The exit-status desk / Illustrated cases
demonstration.title: Three numbers that refuse to mean the same thing.
demonstration.description: Select a case to see what each verification outcome establishes — and what it leaves open. Exit codes are the documented ones, not live measurements.
demonstration.disclaimer: Presentation-only illustrations. No chain is inspected and no finding is produced by this explorer.

cases.title: Exit 0: the record holds together
cases.description: Every record verified against its digest and predecessor.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: proceed to the external checkpoint and signature questions; intactness alone answers neither.

cases.title: Exit 1: the break has a position
cases.description: The first inconsistent record is named with its intact prefix.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: investigate from the break backward. Do not extend the chain while it is broken.

cases.title: Exit 2: no opinion could be formed
cases.description: The input could not be read, parsed or found.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: fix the input, permissions or path first. An unusable check is neither a pass nor a failure of the record.

cases.title: Exit 4: readable destinations disagree
cases.description: Two fan-out checkpoints commit to different tuples.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: treat disagreement as a finding to investigate, not as an outage to retry. Success never implies every destination was checked.

featuredPublication.label: The witness problem / Brief 01
featuredPublication.imageAlt: Three separate evidence questions: the recorded sequence, the signing key, and an external observation.

highlights.label: 01 / Continuity
highlights.title: Know where the record breaks
highlights.text: Report the first inconsistent record and the intact prefix. A malformed input, a broken chain and an unavailable source require different responses.

highlights.label: 02 / Portability
highlights.title: Bytes two languages agree on
highlights.text: The digest is taken over canonical JSON. A Python program using only its standard library can append to and verify a Rust-written nostoi-v1 chain, and the test suite checks the two against each other in both directions.

highlights.label: 03 / Custody
highlights.title: Keep a reference beyond the producer
highlights.text: Compare the chain with a deliberately selected external checkpoint. Conflicting readable destinations fail verification; unavailable destinations are reported as reduced assurance.

sections.title: A record should survive the people and processes that made it.
paragraphs: An automated system can leave behind an immaculate account of events. The harder question is whether that account remained intact after a disputed action, a software change or a change of custody. Nostoi gives reviewers a concrete starting point: inspect the record, verify its structure, and compare it with a reference retained elsewhere.

Its Rust library, command-line tool and terminal interface verify, append, stream and browse audit chains. Each record commits to its own content and to the preceding digest. An inconsistent record at position 204, with positions 1–203 intact, is a finding a reviewer can investigate rather than a single unexplained verdict.

Νόστοι means the homecomings. The name recalls lost Greek epic accounts of journeys home; the project mark depicts the duckling carrying Gretel across the river in Hansel and Gretel. Two different stories, one guiding image: bring something worth preserving across a difficult boundary.

sections.title: One idea, three dialects, one verifier.
paragraphs: Nostoi reads the chains the RAGBAZ projects already keep. nostoi-v1 is its own format, used by Sylvae, by Frog and by anything new; it is a JSON Lines file or the append-only SQLite store. weftmark-ledger-v1 is WeftMark's ledger.jsonl. ephor-audit-v1 is Ephor's governance_events store, hashed over length-prefixed fields rather than canonical JSON. The format is detected; --format overrides it.

The nostoi-v1 record has a consecutive sequence number, a previous digest or sixty-four zeros, an RFC 3339 UTC instant, a required kind, optional actor and subject fields, and a JSON object body. Floating-point values are refused: decimal quantities belong in strings, and integer values must remain within the supported 64-bit range. The canonicalisation contract determines the exact bytes being hashed.

The Python standard-library reference can append and verify nostoi-v1 chains without a Rust build or a native extension. The Rust and Python implementations are checked against each other in both directions. JavaScript consumers must preserve large integer values as JSON text rather than silently rounding them through Number.

sections.title: Put the constraint beneath the application.
paragraphs: The SQLite store retains complete records beside their chain fields. While its schema and triggers remain intact, UPDATE and DELETE are refused, and each INSERT must extend the head with a digest that matches its record. Nostoi registers the required nostoi_digest function; ordinary clients can inspect the file without obtaining a privileged mutation path through the application.

These constraints catch accidental rewrites and application mistakes. They are not an independent witness against someone who controls the database file and can remove the triggers or replace the entire store. That stronger threat model calls for external checkpoints, separate custody and verification outside the producer's control.

Owned databases also declare independent schema revisions and component identities, and prepared requests and kernel payloads carry explicit format tags. nostoi schema PATH --json inspects that metadata without migrating anything, which matters when the question is what a file is rather than how to change it.

sections.title: One destination is one opinion.
paragraphs: An internal check cannot detect a history that was recomputed in full, digests included. That is not a weakness of the hash function; it is what a hash function is for. Detecting it requires a head that was trusted before the rewrite and retained somewhere the rewriter cannot reach.

Replication is useful; administrative independence adds a different protection. Nostoi can publish the same checkpoint to several destinations with separate credentials. Verification checks a deliberately selected key: conflicting readable checkpoints are rejected, while an unreadable destination is explicitly reported as unavailable. A run can succeed with one usable destination, but its assurance then rests on that smaller set.

The durable outbox records the exact prepared request before upload and recovers it after a crash. Publishing and verification use different credential scopes. Retention also has to be examined separately: S3 Object Lock and an operator-configured R2 bucket lock are different mechanisms, and a retention field inside a document is not proof that storage enforces it.

sections.title: Tamper-evident is a useful promise. Tamper-proof would be the wrong one.
paragraphs: Integrity, signer identity and independent observation answer three different questions, and a page that merges them is how provenance pages begin to lie. Did the recorded sequence change? Which key vouched for this statement, and is that key trusted for this purpose? When did somebody else observe it? A chain can answer the first and no part of the others.

Signed attestations address the second. nostoi attest signs a small document with ssh-keygen -Y sign, binding a statement to a head under a verification policy; verify-attestation fails closed on a bad signature, an unpinned key, or a chain that no longer matches. The signer's claimed time inside the statement is not the moment another party saw it. Keeping those apart is the entire discipline.

For the basic chain commands, exit 0 means intact, exit 1 means a broken chain or an append refused on that basis, and exit 2 means a usage or operational error. Anchor fan-out and attestation commands have their own documented outcomes. An intact chain is evidence of internal consistency, not proof that all relevant events were recorded.

sections.title: Small compartments. Inspectable obligations.
paragraphs: nostoi-core contains the formats, canonical JSON, streaming verification and stores. nostoi-anchor owns remote checkpoints and durable upload intents. nostoi-kmsg handles Linux kernel-ring-buffer ingestion. The facade preserves existing nostoi:: paths while portable consumers can select the core without networking, command-line or Linux dependencies.

Native Python and WebAssembly-component bindings reuse that Rust verifier. Current interoperability documentation includes canonical attestation bytes and document-to-chain checks; cryptographic signature verification remains a separate host-side responsibility and is reported as unchecked by those bindings. Registry publication is still pending.

The distinction between a measured result and a general guarantee matters here. A documented three-trial, 250,000-record JSONL run used roughly 3.6 MiB peak resident memory after streaming integration. That is an observation under specified workload and host conditions—not a throughput promise for an operational kernel logger.

sections.title: Rare failure is where dependence becomes visible.
paragraphs: For researchers studying extreme events, the interesting question is not simply how often one service fails. It is which failures arrive together: a shared credential, a common administrator, one software defect, one region-wide outage. Three storage destinations do not justify multiplying three small probabilities unless the relevant independence assumptions have been examined.

Audit quality also affects the observations available for inference. A missing event may be an instrumentation gap, a lost record or a deliberate omission. A valid chain cannot distinguish those explanations by itself. Gaps, retention intervals and checkpoint cadence therefore belong in the analysis alongside verified records.

sections.title: Evidence that can travel beyond the room.
paragraphs: For an investigator examining an agent-mediated action, the useful questions include who authorised it, which system carried it out, which inputs and tools were involved, and what another reviewer can reconstruct. An actor field such as agent:demo is an attribution supplied by the producer. It helps organise the record; it does not authenticate the actor or expose a model's unrecorded reasoning.

For public oversight, ask for an evidence package rather than a reassuring dashboard: the chain and its format, the selected checkpoint and custody, the relevant signature checks, the retained interval, and the known omissions. These are concrete subjects for a procurement specification or an investigation. Legal admissibility, regulatory obligations and proportionality require their own assessment.

The ambition is durable scrutiny of consequential systems. Nostoi supplies one layer of that work: a record another person can check, with its assumptions and gaps still visible. It does not certify an AI system as safe, estimate catastrophic risk, or turn a technically intact history into a complete account of the world.

workflow.title: Name the chain before trusting it
workflow.text: Identify the producer, the format and the purpose. A chain of events is not a chain of true claims. Decide what an intact record would license you to conclude, and write that down first.

workflow.title: Verify, and read the exit status
workflow.text: nostoi verify accepts several paths at once and reports each. Zero is every chain intact; one is a break, or an append refused because the chain was already broken; two is anything else entirely.

workflow.title: Select and retain an external reference
workflow.text: Choose a checkpoint from custody you trust, record its position and digest, and keep it outside the producer's authority. Inspect disagreement and unavailable destinations separately.

workflow.title: Bring the evidence to human review
workflow.text: Attach the checkpoint or the attestation to the wider evidence story. Keep signer trust, external observation and engineering readiness as three separate findings rather than one verdict.

quickstart.title: A small experiment in continuity
quickstart.summary: Build the CLI, create two harmless records, then compare an intact history with a deliberately altered copy. The original remains available as a reference.
quickstart.note: Rust and Python 3 are used below. The altered copy should produce exit 1. Registry publication is pending; production anchoring and signer policy require their own configuration.

commands.label: Build the CLI
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/tabenius/nostoi.git
cd nostoi
cargo build --release --bin nostoi
./target/release/nostoi formats

commands.label: Create, verify, and inspect
commands.code:
./target/release/nostoi append example.jsonl \
  --kind example.start --actor 'you' --body '{"purpose":"learning"}'
./target/release/nostoi append example.jsonl \
  --kind example.finish --actor 'you' --body '{"result":"recorded"}'
./target/release/nostoi verify example.jsonl
./target/release/nostoi head example.jsonl

commands.label: Change the recorded content, not its digest
commands.code:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json
records = [json.loads(line) for line in Path('example.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]
records[0]['body']['purpose'] = 'altered'
Path('altered.jsonl').write_text(''.join(json.dumps(record) + '\n' for record in records))
PY
./target/release/nostoi verify altered.jsonl
printf 'verification exit=%s\n' "$?"
# Expected: exit 1, identifying the first inconsistent record.

pages.title: Three questions behind a trustworthy audit trail
pages.description: Integrity, signer trust and external observation are useful precisely because they are not the same claim.

sections.title: Did the recorded sequence change?
paragraphs: Verify before appending to or acting on a chain. The first inconsistent record is the end of what the evidence can say about continuity: everything before it is accounted for, and nothing after it is established.

A fully recomputed history, or a tail simply removed, evades an internal-only check entirely. That is why a retained external head is not decoration. Compare against a head that was trusted before the change and kept somewhere the rewriter cannot reach.

sections.title: Who signed this statement, and do we trust them for this?
paragraphs: A valid signature binds a statement to a key. It says nothing by itself about whether that key should be believed, or believed for this particular claim about this particular head.

An unverified key label, a sidecar file that happens to sit next to the document, or a signature that has never been checked are not evidence that a check occurred. Verification is an act with a result you can report, not an artefact you can point at.

sections.title: When did somebody else see it?
paragraphs: A signer chooses the timestamp inside its own statement. External observation adds a separate record, with its own source and time. Its evidentiary value depends on that observer's custody and incentives, rather than on an assumption that an outsider has no stake in the outcome.

The resulting evidence can support a WeftMark review, an operator's incident investigation, or a regulator's question about what a system did. It still cannot prove that every statement in the underlying chain is true, and a page that implies otherwise has taken a small liberty with a large subject.

sections.title: How to read a failure without being misled by it
paragraphs: Read the exit status before the text. Zero means intact. One means a break, or an append correctly refused. Two means the tool could not form an opinion: an unreadable file, a malformed record, a missing table.

Then read the sequence number. Record 204 altered with 1 to 203 intact is a different situation from a file that fails to parse, and a different situation again from a chain that verifies because it is empty. Nostoi reports these separately because collapsing them destroys the part of the finding that a reader can act on.

pages.title: The witness problem: independence without a majority vote
pages.description: Copies, separate custody and agreeing observations provide different kinds of assurance. Nostoi makes their failure states explicit.

sections.title: Replicas are not witnesses
paragraphs: Suppose a history is rewritten and the new head is copied to two more places. Every copy agrees, and every copy was written by whoever performed the rewrite. Agreement between them carries no information about whether the rewrite happened.

Copies can improve availability and protect against some storage failures. Their value against a malicious rewrite depends on whether one authority can replace all of them. Replica count and independent custody therefore belong in different columns of the assessment.

sections.title: Independence is a property of administration, not of geography
paragraphs: Separate administrators, credential scopes, providers and retention controls can reduce common failure paths. None makes an observer incorruptible. Two regions in one account may still share the same administrator and credentials; different providers may still depend on one publisher host or one compromised operator.

Nostoi anchors to several destinations with per-destination credentials, and separates the credential that publishes from the one that verifies, alongside an independently selected trusted checkpoint key. A reader can therefore ask a sharper question than is-this-stored: who could have written this, and who checked it.

sections.title: Requiring agreement, and what it costs
paragraphs: Nostoi's fan-out verifier is not a majority-vote protocol. Readable destinations must agree on the chain, format, sequence and digest; conflicting tuples produce exit 4. No usable destination is a failure. If at least one confirms the chain and the others are unavailable rather than conflicting, verification can succeed with an explicit reduced-assurance warning.

That policy separates a contradiction from an outage. It also means success alone does not imply that every configured destination was checked. A deployment requiring a minimum number of independent witnesses must enforce that requirement in its operational policy; it should not infer it from the exit code.

sections.title: What this means for an investigator or a regulator
paragraphs: An investigator wants to know whether a record existed before a disputed change. A single retained head answers that for a window that ends when the holder's copy is rewritten. Independent anchors extend that window, and make it harder for one party to unwrite its own history.

These observations can make a rewrite detectable relative to a retained checkpoint. They do not automatically identify the person who changed it, authenticate the original event, or establish legal admissibility. Attribution and a defensible time of observation need additional evidence.

pages.title: Canonical bytes are a portability contract
pages.description: A digest is only useful if two implementations agree on the bytes before hashing. That agreement has to be specified, not assumed.

sections.title: What is hashed, exactly
paragraphs: The digest is the SHA-256, lowercase hex, of the record without its digest field, encoded as canonical JSON: keys in code point order, no whitespace, and strings escaped only where the specification says so. Not the file as it happens to sit on your disk. Not a pretty-printed object. Not a JSON object with the fields in the order you happened to write them.

Getting this exactly right is the entire difference between a chain two languages can share and a chain that verifies only on the machine that made it. Every divergence that looks cosmetic is a divergence that will surface as a broken chain in someone else's timezone.

sections.title: Why there are no floating-point numbers
paragraphs: A record body may not contain floats. Their textual representation differs between languages and even between versions of the same language, so two correct implementations can serialise the same value differently and produce different digests for identical content.

The rule is to write decimals as strings. This is a small inconvenience at authoring time and a permanent one avoided later, and it is the clearest example of a portability constraint that looks pedantic until the first cross-language test fails.

sections.title: Proving it, rather than intending it
paragraphs: The test suite checks the Rust implementation against the Python reference in both directions: chains written in one verify in the other. The reference uses Python's standard library, providing an independent implementation without a native extension.

Native Python bindings, a versioned WIT component and generated JavaScript and TypeScript bindings exist in the checkout. The current binding contract supports canonical attestation bytes and checking a document against a chain, with signature state explicitly unchecked. Host-side signature verification is a separate responsibility; registry publication remains pending.

sections.title: What canonical bytes do not buy
paragraphs: Agreement on serialisation is not agreement on meaning. Two parties can encode the same bytes while describing entirely different events, and a chain will faithfully preserve that ambiguity.

It also says nothing about who produced a record. Canonical form makes the content checkable; it does not make it authentic. Authentication is a separate question with separate machinery, and a system that answers the first and is assumed to answer the second has a gap exactly where it is least likely to be noticed.

pages.title: At the edge of the distribution: dependence and missing evidence
pages.description: Why correlated failures and incomplete observations matter when an audit trail is used to study rare, consequential events.

sections.title: Count failure domains, not destinations.
paragraphs: If compromise events A and B were independent, their joint probability would be P(A)P(B). Independence is an assumption, not a property conferred by choosing two bucket names. A shared identity provider, credential, administrator, deployment pipeline or verification host can couple the failures.

Nostoi's multi-destination anchoring helps organise custody and expose conflicting observations. It does not estimate a joint failure distribution or claim a quantified reduction in catastrophic risk. Any numerical argument needs assumptions about common causes, evidence supporting those assumptions, and sensitivity to their failure.

sections.title: An intact sample is not necessarily an unbiased one.
paragraphs: A chain verifies the records it contains. It cannot establish that the producer included every relevant action, that a sensor was running during an outage, or that omitted observations resemble retained ones. If consequential failures preferentially interrupt logging, the missingness mechanism matters to any statistical interpretation.

A serious review therefore describes capture coverage, observed gaps, retention and checkpoint cadence alongside chain-integrity results. An external checkpoint bounds what can be silently rewritten relative to that reference; it does not recover events that were never recorded.

sections.title: A percentile is not a theory of the tail.
paragraphs: The repository reports per-trial p50, p95 and p99 native append latencies, together with the largest observed samples and durability settings. Those are empirical summaries of a specified experiment. They do not determine an extreme-value distribution, a return period or a bound on the worst possible stall.

For workload or hazard analysis, retain the experiment's scope: record sizes, sample counts, host conditions, synchronisation policy and whether observations were pooled. An audit mechanism is useful when it helps preserve those distinctions, rather than converting measurements into a universal performance claim.

sections.title: Ask questions that an evidence package can answer.
paragraphs: For an investigation or a public procurement, specify the retained interval, the exported format, who controls capture, where checkpoints live, which keys were trusted, and how outages and contradictions are reported. Ask what was verified by an independent party and what remains the producer's assertion.

This is a technical contribution to accountable oversight, not an automatic conclusion about compliance with any particular law. Records can contain personal or confidential information; access, retention and disclosure must match the actual purpose of the investigation.
